items.recapEn: Hana and Ken climbed from Odawara into Hakone's mist. At the checkpoint by Lake Ashi, Satō-san, dressed in a kimono, asked to see their tickets; inside, a boy ate a black egg and Ken photographed one. Fuji stayed hidden. By the hotel's hot spring Hana wrote: Fuji is there, just not showing its face. Tanaka-san has predicted a clear morning.

items.recapEn: In the corridor after the bath, Ken tells Hana it is raining again and asks to see her notebook; she is writing down what he says, plain forms and all. He is eating a black egg and wants salt, which is in his own pack. Tanaka-san has promised Fuji tomorrow, so Hana expects it to hide but will look anyway.

items.recapEn: Hakone Checkpoint notice: buy a ticket at the entrance (500 yen, 250 for children), leave big bags beside the door, wait and enter one at a time, show your ticket to the person in the kimono, do not run in the old buildings, eat and drink outside, photos by Lake Ashi, and bring a jacket—Hakone is cold even in summer.
